source_text: Ἡμῶν γὰρ πάντων δεδιότων καὶ τῆς σαρκίνης δεσποίνης αὐτῆς, ἥτις ἦν καὶ αὐτὴ τῶν μαρτύρων μία ἀγωνίστρια, ἀγωνιώσης μὴ οὐδὲ τὴν ὁμολογίαν δυνήσεται παρρησιάσασθαι διὰ τὸ ἀσθενὲς τοῦ σώματος, ἡ Βλανδῖνα τοσαύτης ἐπληρώθη δυνάμεως ὥστε ἐκλυθῆναι καὶ παρεθῆναι τοὺς κατὰ διαδοχὰς παντὶ τρόπῳ βασανίζοντας αὐτὴν ἀπὸ ἑωθινῆς ἕως ἑσπέρας, καὶ αὐτοὺς ὁμολογοῦντας ὅτι νενίκηνται μηδὲν ἔχοντες μηκέτι ὃ ποιήσωσιν αὐτῇ, καὶ θαυμάζειν ἐπὶ τῷ παραμένειν ἔμπνουν αὐτήν, παντὸς τοῦ σώματος περιερρωγότος καὶ ἠνεῳγμένου, καὶ μαρτυρεῖν ὅτι ἓν εἶδος στρεβλώσεως ἱκανὸν ἦν πρὸς τὸ ἐξαγαγεῖν τὴν ψυχήν, οὐχ ὅτι γε τοιαῦτα καὶ τοσαῦτα. Ἀλλ᾽ ἡ μακαρία ὡς γενναῖος ἀθλητὴς ἀνενέαζεν ἐν τῇ ὁμολογίᾳ, καὶ ἦν αὐτῆς ἀνάληψις καὶ ἀνάπαυσις καὶ ἀναλγησία τῶν συμβαινόντων τὸ λέγειν ὅτι· Χριστιανή εἰμι καὶ παρ᾽ ἡμῖν οὐδὲν φαῦλον γίνεται.
pass_a_gloss: For with all of us fearing, and with her fleshly mistress — who was herself also one champion of the martyrs — being in anguish lest she might not even be able to speak out the confession because of the weakness of her body, Blandina was filled with so much power that those torturing her by turns in every way from morning until evening grew loose and gave way, themselves confessing that they had been defeated, having no longer anything that they might do to her, and wondering that she remained breathing, with her whole body torn all around and opened up, and bearing witness that one kind of racking was sufficient to bring out the soul, to say nothing of such and so many. But the blessed one, as a noble athlete, was made young again in the confession, and her taking-up and rest and freedom from pain amid the things happening was the saying: I am a Christian and among us nothing base is done.
pass_b_english: For while we were all afraid, and her mistress according to the flesh, who was herself also one of the contending martyrs, was in anguish lest she should not even be able to utter her confession boldly because of the feebleness of her body, Blandina was filled with such power that those who tortured her in every way in succession from dawn to evening grew faint and withdrew, themselves admitting that they were conquered and had nothing left that they could do to her, and marveling that she remained breathing when her whole body was torn and laid open, and declaring that a single kind of torment was enough to drive out the soul, let alone such and so many torments.

But the blessed woman, like a noble athlete, took new strength in her confession, and her renewal and rest and deadening of the pain of what befell her lay in saying, I am a Christian, and no evil is done among us.

choices.why: σαρκίνης qualifies an earthly household relation, contrasted with spiritual kinship in the narrative, so rendered as a relational phrase rather than a material adjective.
adverbial phrase with the participle shows relays of torturers replacing one another through the day, not rank or order.

choices.english: renewal and rest and deadening of pain
choices.why: three nouns in series describe her recovery in confession; ἀναλγησία is privative, so it must mean absence of pain rather than endurance of it.
